findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py (_local_labels, hop_is_local, validate_local_fallbacks) treats a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` as a valid local label and the loader admits it. cheval.py's _build_provider_config only reads dispatch_group from the model entry, so ModelConfig.dispatch_group is None for such hops and openai_adapter._transport_policy returns None. audit/modelinv.hop_locality_of likewise only reads the model entry.
findings.description: A provider whose block (not its model entries) declares `dispatch_group: local` passes the loader's local-hop rule, but the adapter never sees the label. For an https local endpoint without `allow_insecure_endpoint`, no TransportPolicy is applied: proxy environment variables are honoured, the urllib fallback follows redirects, and the request URL is not held to the declared path. The MODELINV row records hop_locality `hosted` for a hop the loader (and the planner under `local_voices`) considers local, so the locality audit trail disagrees with the enforcement point.
findings.failure_mode: Operator sets `dispatch_group: local` at the provider level (accepted at load) and runs under `locality: local_voices`. An HTTPS_PROXY in the environment, or a 3xx from the local server, carries the prompt to a non-local host with no request-time refusal, and the audit log labels the hop hosted rather than flagging the discrepancy.
findings.suggested_fix: In _build_provider_config fall back to prov.get("dispatch_group") when the model entry is silent (matching hop_is_local), and have hop_locality_of delegate to endpoint_policy.hop_is_local so one implementation decides locality at load, request time and emit time.

findings.cross_file_justification: TransportPolicy is constructed only in providers/openai_adapter.py (_transport_policy, health_check). validate_providers admits `allow_insecure_endpoint` on any provider type; types.ProviderConfig.allow_insecure_endpoint is set for all types in cheval._build_provider_config. Other HTTP adapters (anthropic/bedrock, implied by compliance_profile and auth_modes) are not shown to consume policy.
findings.description: The load-time half of D-7.2 is type-agnostic: any HTTP provider may carry an `http://` endpoint once it names a loopback/RFC1918 opt-in. The request-time half (no proxy env, no redirects, path-prefix rule) is wired only into OpenAIAdapter. A non-OpenAI-type provider that opts in gets a plaintext endpoint with none of the compensating controls the docstring promises, and its health probe uses the unpoliced path.
findings.failure_mode: An `anthropic`-type provider is configured with `endpoint: http://10.0.0.5:8080` and the matching opt-in. The config loads cleanly. Requests honour HTTP_PROXY, and under the urllib fallback a redirect from the local server is followed with the Authorization header intact, possibly to a public host.
findings.suggested_fix: Either refuse `allow_insecure_endpoint` (and `dispatch_group: local`) at load for provider types whose adapter does not implement TransportPolicy, or move policy construction into ProviderAdapter base so every adapter's http_post/http_post_stream call receives it.

findings.anchor: _open = _policy_urllib_opener().open if policy is not None else urllib.request.urlopen
findings.description: The diff introduces a redirect-refusing, proxy-free urllib opener but applies it only when a TransportPolicy is present. Hosted providers on the urllib fallback keep urllib.request.urlopen, whose default HTTPRedirectHandler follows 3xx responses, preserves the Authorization header on the new request, and permits an https→http scheme downgrade. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so the two transports now diverge on redirect handling for hosted hops. Pre-existing behaviour, but the diff is the point where the safe opener was added and deliberately not applied.
findings.failure_mode: A hosted or compromised OpenAI-compatible gateway answers 302 to an attacker host. Under the urllib fallback the bearer API key is re-sent to that host, potentially over plaintext.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the no-redirect opener unconditionally for urllib (redirects are already an error on the httpx path), or at minimum refuse cross-origin and scheme-downgrading redirects for every provider rather than only opted-in ones.

findings.description: Any HTTP 400 whose body contains the substring `response_format` or `json_schema` (any field, any case) causes the adapter to drop the strict schema and re-send the full prompt once. A server controls both the status and the body, so a server can unilaterally downgrade structured output to unenforced mode and receive the prompt twice. The downgrade is recorded (schema_rejected_by_server, schema_enforced=false), which is why this is low rather than medium.
findings.failure_mode: A misbehaving or hostile OpenAI-compatible server returns 400 with an error message that merely mentions response_format. cheval retries without the schema, the answer is parsed by the tolerant path, and the caller relies on downstream repair instead of server-enforced structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the heuristic to the error object's `param`/`code` fields rather than a whole-body substring match, and consider making the schema-less retry opt-in per model (e.g. only when `structured_json` is declared with a `retry_without_schema` flag).

findings.description: describe_provider claims it never carries a secret, but it emits the post-interpolation `endpoint` verbatim to stdout for model-health-probe.sh. The loader interpolates `{env:...}` templates into any string, so an operator who templates a token into the endpoint path or query (a common pattern for some gateways) has it printed by the probe CLI and captured in probe logs. Userinfo is refused by the validator, but path and query components are not.
findings.failure_mode: Config has `endpoint: https://gw.example.com/{env:GW_TENANT_KEY}/v1`. `python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy describe-provider gw` prints the resolved key to stdout, which the probe script captures.
findings.suggested_fix: Return only scheme, canonical host and port (via split_url) from describe_provider, or pass the endpoint through redact_config / the raw pre-interpolation value as is done for `auth`.
